text:
sathya: seeing intermittent packet loss on overlay in us-west-2 gpu-pool — pod->pod latency spikes and ~0.3-1% packet drops during large model pulls and grpc traffic. started ~2026-03-15 01:40 UTC. tcpdump shows retransmits and some truncated IP lengths. anyone seen this pattern?
jen: did anything change at infra level? MTU, ENI, or recent kernel upgrades?
maya: can you paste a short tcpdump output and node name? also are these all on same AZ?
sathya: node ip-10-0-3-12 and ip-10-0-3-18, same AZ. sample tcpdump snippet below:
```
17:03:12.123456 IP 10.0.3.12 > 10.0.3.18: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 229, length 1460
17:03:12.123789 IP 10.0.3.12 > 10.0.3.18: frag 0, proto TCP (6), length 1500
17:03:12.124000 IP 10.0.3.12 > 10.0.3.18: Flags [F.], seq 3000:4460, ack 2000, win 229, length 1460
# then a bunch of retransmits and some "bad checksum" on capture on the receiving host
```
jen: looks like packets are being cut at the overlay boundary. check host MTU vs VNI MTU and the kernel offload settings (GSO/TCP segmentation offload).
leo: common culprit is GSO+VXLAN + certain kernel versions + ENI driver. can you check ethtool and sysctl?
maya: run these on both hosts:
```
ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'gso|tso|gro|lro'
ethtool -S eth0 | head -n 40
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward net.core.rmem_max net.core.rmem_default net.core.rmem_max
ip link show dev geneve0 || ip link show dev vxlan0
```
sathya: ethtool shows GSO/TSO on. geneve0 MTU 1450, host eth0 MTU 9001. weird mismatch.
jen: that MTU mismatch will cause encapsulated packets to exceed outer MTU and lead to fragmentation or truncation if offloads are active. if GSO is on, kernel expects NIC to do segmentation; with an overlay it can result in broken fragments.
net-bot: alerted: node ip-10-0-3-12 egress qdisc backlog > 1.2s for pod cidr 10.244.2.0/24 (2026-03-15T01:42:00Z).
oncall-bot: deploy/dataset-cache-rollout started for gpu-pool (triggered by sathya)
leo: quick mitigation: disable GSO/TSO on the host for the physical NIC or set VNI MTU to match outer MTU. you can do: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off` — that removed the truncation for me in a similar incident.
maya: also consider bumping outer MTU to 9000 everywhere end-to-end (ENI + host + overlay) but aws ENI jumbo frames vary by instance type/ENI. confirm provider limits.
sathya: tried `ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off` on ip-10-0-3-12 and run end-to-end tests — packet loss dropped to ~0.02% and grpc retries disappeared for now.
jen: good. long-term fix: either align MTUs across host+overlay or use a kernel driver patch/workaround. which kernel are you on?
sathya: nodes are on 5.15.0-98-amd64 (recent managed image).
leo: there were a couple of regressions around GSO+VXLAN in 5.15.x and some cloud provider ENI drivers. options: kernel upgrade to patched release or pin to older stable if safe. also consider enabling GRO fixups for vxlan if backport available.
maya: we should also verify conntrack and iptables rules aren't dropping large flows. run `conntrack -L | grep <pod-ip>` if needed.
sathya: conntrack entries look normal. issue correlates strongly with >1MB transfers (model shard pulls) so it's likely segmentation/offload.
jen: create small canary that does continuous 6MB transfers between pods while we iterate. run `iperf -M 1440 -c <peer>` and `curl --limit-rate` style tests.
sathya: will run canary across 6 nodes in the pool. posting results shortly.
oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-342: "overlay seg-offload truncation in us-west-2 gpu-pool"
leo: follow-up actions: 1) temporary cluster-wide GSO disable on worker eth0 in gpu-pool OR set vni MTU to 1400 2) schedule kernel/eni driver upgrade test 3) add MTU/ethtool health check to node exporter 4) route model pulls via node-local cache to reduce large east-west bursts
maya: + add CI test for large chunked transfers across overlay to catch regressions in future kernel/image updates.
sathya: thanks all — pushing hotfix (GSO off) and will update incident INC-2026-342 with telemetry and rollback plan. :thumbsup:
jen: if this recurs after kernel upgrade we may need to coordinate with provider for ENI firmware. keep me posted.
leo: noted. I'll make a runbook entry and a short postmortem template once we confirm root cause.
